# rosettacommons/foundry (commit b02eed6a6bdf8f44d14a80cc36e3da13c9f2291c)
# rosettacommons/foundry Overview
The Foundry repository provides a collection of biomolecular design models. It offers tools for inverse folding, *de novo* design, and structure prediction across proteins, ligands, and nucleic acids. These models integrate into a common framework for efficient biomolecular engineering.

The framework includes Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) models for inverse folding and sequence design. These models, including [`ProteinMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21), [`LigandMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2303), and [`SolubleMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2173), generate amino acid sequences for protein backbones or sequences that bind to specific ligands. They utilize graph featurization, message passing layers, and decoding strategies to process structural information and predict optimal sequences. Further details are available in [Protein and Ligand Inverse Folding (MPNN)](#protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn).

For structure prediction, Foundry incorporates RoseTTAFold3 (RF3). This model predicts three-dimensional protein structures from amino acid sequences. RF3 uses a diffusion-based generative approach and includes confidence estimation, providing Predicted Local Distance Difference Test (pLDDT) and Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) metrics for assessment. Learn more in [RoseTTAFold3 (RF3) for Structure Prediction](#rosettafold3-rf3-for-structure-prediction).

RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) supports *de novo* biomolecular interaction design. This generative diffusion model creates novel proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules with desired binding properties. It employs iterative denoising and allows users to define design constraints through an [`InputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L112) for elements like [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) regions, [`ligand`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L142) specifications, and [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) methods. More information is in [RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) for De Novo Design](#rfdiffusion3-rfd3-for-de-novo-design).

An extension of RFD3, RFdiffusion3NA (RFD3NA), supports multipolymer design, handling complex protein-DNA-RNA systems. It offers specialized [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) specifications for nucleic acids and advanced [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) for detailed control over residue and atom selections. This includes constraints for nucleic acid secondary structure and base-pairing, and integration of symmetry operations. Details are available in [RFdiffusion3NA (RFD3NA) for Multipolymer Design](#rfdiffusion3na-rfd3na-for-multipolymer-design).

The Foundry core library provides the foundational infrastructure for machine learning workflows. It manages configuration, training harnesses, inference engines, evaluation metrics, and callback systems. These components ensure a structured approach to building and deploying biomolecular design models. Refer to [Foundry Core Library and ML Workflows](#foundry-core-library-and-ml-workflows) for additional details.

Command-line interface (CLI) tools simplify management of the Foundry ecosystem. They allow users to install, list, and clean model checkpoints. This ensures consistent and reproducible model usage. Additional information is available in [Command Line Interface (CLI) Utilities](#command-line-interface-cli-utilities).

## Introduction to Foundry Models
The Foundry framework provides a collection of biomolecular design models, each tailored for specific tasks in protein, ligand, and nucleic acid engineering. These models address key challenges in structural biology, such as inverse folding, *de novo* design, and protein folding prediction.

For inverse folding and sequence design, the framework includes re-implementations of the widely used ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN models. These models are designed to generate amino acid sequences for a given protein backbone structure, or to design sequences that bind to specific ligands, respectively. The core functionality of these models involves graph featurization and message passing layers to process structural information and predict optimal sequences. Further details on the architecture and functionality can be found in [Protein and Ligand Inverse Folding (MPNN) Architecture and Core Functionality](#introduction-to-foundry-models-protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-architecture-and-core-functionality). Data preparation and training infrastructure are described in [MPNN Data Preparation and Training Pipelines](#introduction-to-foundry-models-mpnn-data-preparation-and-training-pipelines), while inference and evaluation metrics are covered in [MPNN Inference and Evaluation](#introduction-to-foundry-models-mpnn-inference-and-evaluation).

For protein folding prediction, Foundry incorporates RoseTTAFold3 (RF3), which predicts the three-dimensional structure of proteins from their amino acid sequences. This model integrates advanced structural components and a diffusion module to refine predictions, and it can include confidence estimation for the predicted structures. The intricate architecture of RF3, including its confidence estimation capabilities, is explored in [RF3 Model Architecture and Confidence Estimation](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rf3-model-architecture-and-confidence-estimation). Advanced data processing, kinematic calculations, and diverse input handling are detailed in [RF3 Advanced Data Processing and Kinematics](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rf3-advanced-data-processing-and-kinematics), and the loss functions and evaluation metrics guiding its training are outlined in [RF3 Loss Functions and Evaluation Metrics](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rf3-loss-functions-and-evaluation-metrics).

The framework also features RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), a generative diffusion model for *de novo* biomolecular interaction design. RFD3 excels at creating novel proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules with desired binding properties. It employs an iterative denoising process to generate designs, and its [`InputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L112) allows for precise control over design constraints, such as defining specific contig regions or ligand interactions. The diffusion process and input specification are further discussed in [RFD3 Diffusion Process and Input Specification](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3-diffusion-process-and-input-specification), and its training and advanced conditioning strategies are described in [RFD3 Training and Advanced Conditioning](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3-training-and-advanced-conditioning).

An extension of RFD3, RFdiffusion3NA (RFD3NA), provides comprehensive capabilities for multipolymer design, handling complex protein-DNA-RNA systems. This model offers specialized [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) specifications for nucleic acids and advanced [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) for detailed control over residue and atom selections, including secondary structure and base-pairing constraints for nucleic acid designs. The multipolymer [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) specification and input selection are detailed in [RFD3NA Multipolymer Contig Specification and Input Selection](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3na-multipolymer-contig-specification-and-input-selection). Extensive data transformations and symmetry operations essential for maintaining structural integrity in multipolymer design are elaborated in [RFD3NA Data Transforms and Symmetry Operations](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3na-data-transforms-and-symmetry-operations).

These models are integrated into the broader Foundry ecosystem, leveraging shared utilities for configuration, training, and inference. The ecosystem provides a robust foundation for biomolecular structure manipulation and processing, enabling researchers and engineers to develop and apply these advanced models effectively.

### Protein and Ligand Inverse Folding (MPNN) Architecture and Core Functionality
The ProteinMPNN model, implemented in the [`ProteinMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) class found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py), is designed for protein sequence prediction based on 3D structural information. This model, along with its ligand-aware variant ([`LigandMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2303)), processes protein coordinates and residue masks to output amino acid sequences. Its architecture is composed of several key stages: graph featurization, message passing layers, positional encoding, and sequence decoding strategies.

Graph featurization transforms raw atomic coordinates and residue identities into a graph representation suitable for neural network processing. The [`ProteinFeatures`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L11) class within [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py) is central to this process. It extracts features such as 3D coordinates, computes pairwise distances between residues, and applies radial basis function (RBF) embeddings to convert these distances into a higher-dimensional representation. This module also handles the extraction of specific atom types (e.g., backbone atoms) and can generate virtual atoms for more abstract structural representations. Specialized subclasses like [`ProteinFeaturesMembrane`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L791), [`ProteinFeaturesPSSM`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L849), and [`ProteinFeaturesLigand`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L897) extend this base functionality to incorporate additional information such as membrane context, position-specific scoring matrix (PSSM) data, or complex protein-ligand interaction features, respectively. These extensions allow the model to adapt to a wider range of biomolecular design problems by generating more specific node and edge features.

Following featurization, the model employs message passing layers to integrate information across the protein graph. The encoder ([`EncLayer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L114)) and decoder ([`DecLayer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L227)), defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py), use these features to iteratively update node and edge embeddings. These layers aggregate information from neighboring nodes and edges, allowing the model to develop a comprehensive understanding of the protein's structural and chemical environment. Positional encoding, managed by the [`PositionalEncodings`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py#L5) class in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py), provides chain-aware embeddings that capture the relative positions of residues, ensuring that spatial and sequential relationships are preserved throughout the message passing process.

Sequence design is achieved through decoding strategies. During training, [`decode_teacher_forcing`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L986) uses the known ground truth sequence to guide the model's predictions, which helps stabilize learning. For inference, [`decode_auto_regressive`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L1259) iteratively predicts residues in a specified order, using previously predicted residues as context. This iterative approach allows for the generation of novel protein sequences. Both decoding methods utilize dynamically generated causality masks ([`causal_mask`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L373), [`anti_causal_mask`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L375)) to control the flow of information, preventing the model from accessing future information during prediction and ensuring adherence to autoregressive principles. The model also incorporates mechanisms to handle sequence symmetry, adjusting the decoding order and aggregating logits across symmetric residues to ensure consistent and biologically plausible designs. The [`logits_to_sample`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L872) function converts raw model outputs into sampled sequences, allowing control over sequence diversity through parameters such as [`temperature`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/README.md#L122) and [`bias`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L225).

### MPNN Data Preparation and Training Pipelines
The data preparation and transformation pipelines for MPNN models are designed to convert raw structural data into a format suitable for model input, supporting both training and inference. The [`build_mpnn_transform_pipeline`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py#L61) function, located in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py), constructs a [`Compose`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/utils/rigid.py#L626) object that orchestrates a series of transformations. This pipeline allows for conditional processing, applying specific transformations based on whether the data is for training or inference, and whether the model type is [`protein_mpnn`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L154) or [`ligand_mpnn`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L155).

The pipeline begins with data filtering and preprocessing, including the removal of hydrogen atoms and the handling of undesired residue tokens. It then proceeds with atomization and residue indexing, which involves adding within-chain residue indices, handling covalent modifications, and flagging non-polymeric components for atomization. Occupancy-based masking is used to filter out residues with unresolved backbone atoms. Crucially, the [`FeaturizeUserSettings`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py#L21) class in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py) prepares user-defined parameters, such as [`structure_noise`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L1995) for data augmentation during training and [`decode_type`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L1998) for inference, integrating them into the model's features. Interface computation for ligand models is managed by [`ComputePolymerLigandInterface`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py#L17) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py), which identifies and marks polymer atoms interacting with ligands, and [`FeaturizePolymerLigandInterfaceMask`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py#L16) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py), which generates a residue-level mask for these interactions.

The training infrastructure, orchestrated by the script in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py), sets up the environment for training MPNN models. This includes defining a NoamOpt-style learning rate scheduler to dynamically adjust the learning rate during training. Datasets are prepared using [`StructuralDatasetWrapper`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L9), which integrates with [`GenericDFParser`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L10) for structural data and applies the transformation pipelines. For efficient training, particularly with variable-length protein sequences, [`PaddedTokenBudgetBatchSampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py#L9) from [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py) creates batches based on a token budget, optimizing GPU memory usage. A [`TokenBudgetAwareFeatureCollator`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py#L187) from [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py) combines samples into batches while respecting token budget constraints.

The [`MPNNTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py) manages the overall training and validation loops. It handles model construction, loss calculation, and metric computation. The primary loss function used is [`LabelSmoothedNLLLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py#L7) from [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py), a negative log-likelihood loss with label smoothing to improve generalization. The training setup also includes checkpointing functionality to save and load model states, facilitating continued training and reproducibility.

### MPNN Inference and Evaluation
The MPNN inference engine is responsible for executing protein and ligand sequence design using trained MPNN models. This engine, implemented in the [`MPNNInferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) class found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py), streamlines the process from loading a model to generating and evaluating designed sequences.

The inference engine initializes by configuring parameters such as the [`model_type`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L26) (e.g., [`protein_mpnn`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L154) or [`ligand_mpnn`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L155)), the [`checkpoint_path`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference.py#L31) for loading pre-trained weights, and various output settings. It automatically detects the available computing device (CUDA, XPU, MPS, or CPU) to ensure compatibility across different hardware environments. A key capability of the engine is its support for loading both standard and "legacy" model weights. Legacy weights, often originating from earlier versions of ProteinMPNN, require specific transformations to ensure compatibility with the current refactored model architecture. This involves renaming parameters, adjusting atom type embeddings, and reordering pairwise backbone distance and amino acid token embeddings, as handled by the [`load_legacy_weights`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py#L20) function in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py).

During inference, the [`run`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L273) method of the engine processes input structures, which can be provided as dictionaries or [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects. For each input, it constructs a transformation pipeline to prepare the data for the model. This pipeline performs tasks such as cleaning structures, atomization, featurization of user settings, and calculation of polymer-ligand interfaces, drawing on components defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms). The prepared data is then fed to the MPNN model for a forward pass.

Following model execution, the engine decodes the predicted sequences from the model's output. The designed sequences, along with per-residue confidence scores, are used to update the input [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects. An important step here involves removing non-backbone, non-atomized, and non-fixed atoms from the original structure that are replaced by the newly designed side chains. The entire process is controlled programmatically or via a command-line interface (CLI) provided by [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference.py), which uses utilities in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py) for argument parsing and JSON configuration management. The [`MPNNInferenceInput`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py#L681) dataclass in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py) plays a crucial role in validating input parameters, applying default values, and annotating [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects with MPNN-specific metadata like designed residue masks, temperature settings, and bias vectors.

Evaluation of the designed sequences is an integral part of the inference process. The engine utilizes a [`MetricManager`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/metrics/metric.py#L40) to compute various metrics, providing quantitative insights into the model's performance. These metrics, defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics), include:
*   **Negative Log Likelihood (NLL)** and **Perplexity**: Calculated by [`NLL`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L14), [`InterfaceNLL`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L222), [`SampledNLL`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L397), and [`SampledLigandInterfaceNLL`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L442) classes in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py). These metrics quantify how well the model predicts the ground truth or sampled sequences, with specialized versions for residues at the polymer-ligand interface.
*   **Confidence Scores**: [`MPNNConfidence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L495) and [`MPNNLigandInterfaceConfidence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L539) (also in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py)) derive confidence values from the NLL of sampled sequences, indicating the model's certainty in its predictions.
*   **Sequence Recovery**: The [`SequenceRecovery`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py#L14) and [`InterfaceSequenceRecovery`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py#L294) classes in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py) measure the percentage of correctly predicted residues, again with specialized versions for interface residues.

Finally, the [`MPNNInferenceOutput`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py#L2206) dataclass in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py) encapsulates the results of each inference run. It allows for writing the designed [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) to CIF files and generated sequences to FASTA files, optionally including metadata such as confidence and sequence recovery in the FASTA headers. For further details on the architecture and core functionalities of the MPNN models themselves, refer to [Protein and Ligand Inverse Folding (MPNN) Architecture and Core Functionality](#introduction-to-foundry-models-protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-architecture-and-core-functionality). The data preparation and training aspects are described in [MPNN Data Preparation and Training Pipelines](#introduction-to-foundry-models-mpnn-data-preparation-and-training-pipelines).

### RF3 Model Architecture and Confidence Estimation
The RoseTTAFold3 (RF3) model, implemented primarily in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py), provides a framework for biomolecular structure prediction, employing a diffusion-based generative approach. The core [`RF3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L56) class integrates several key components to achieve this. A [`FeatureInitializer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L401) sets up the initial token-level representations, which are then refined through a [`Recycler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L257) mechanism. This [`Recycler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L257) iteratively processes sequence and pair representations, contributing to the model's ability to refine its understanding of the molecular context over multiple passes. The central generative aspect is handled by the [`DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L70), which takes noisy atomic coordinates and other features to iteratively predict an update, essentially denoising the structure. Finally, a [`DistogramHead`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L233) predicts inter-residue distance distributions, providing a probabilistic representation of pairwise distances. During inference, an [`inference_sampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54) orchestrates the full diffusion rollout, generating a complete predicted structure.

The architecture of [`RF3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L56) allows for flexible prediction modes within the [`DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L70) to predict either the original clean data, the noise, or a correction based on the input noisy coordinates, offering versatility in how the diffusion process is controlled. The model processes information at both fine-grained atom-level and coarse-grained token-level. An [`AtomAttentionDecoder`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L33) translates higher-level token features into atom-level updates for positions, while [`DiffusionConditioning`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L174) prepares dynamic features for the [`DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L70) by incorporating diffusion time and input features.

For assessing the reliability of its predictions, the RF3 framework includes [`RF3WithConfidence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L334), an extension that adds explicit confidence estimation capabilities. This class integrates a [`ConfidenceHead`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py#L25) (defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py)) to predict quality metrics such as predicted Local Distance Difference Test (pLDDT) and Predicted Aligned Error (PAE). These metrics offer insights into the accuracy of the predicted local structure and the relative alignment of domains, respectively. [`RF3WithConfidence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L334) also incorporates a [`mini_rollout_sampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L340) for faster diffusion rollouts, primarily used during training to estimate confidence without the computational cost of a full inference run. Critically, it supports an early stopping mechanism, which can halt the iterative recycling process during inference if confidence metrics reach a sufficient threshold, optimizing computational resources. The [`ConfidenceHead`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py#L25) calculates these metrics by processing latent representations, predicted atom coordinates, and sequence information, using techniques like distance discretization and optionally incorporating Cb distances for enhanced feature representation.

### RF3 Advanced Data Processing and Kinematics
The RF3 model incorporates advanced data processing pipelines and kinematic calculations to handle diverse input formats and execute complex geometric transformations essential for biomolecular structure prediction.

Data preparation in RF3 is managed by a comprehensive pipeline constructed by [`build_af3_transform_pipeline`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L129) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py). This pipeline processes raw structural data through various transformations, including [`RemoveHydrogens`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L84) and [`HandleUndesiredResTokens`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L82) for standardization. Key annotations for indexing and identification, such as [`AddGlobalAtomIdAnnotation`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L20) and [`AddGlobalTokenIdAnnotation`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L4), are added. Non-polymer residues undergo atomization via [`AtomizeByCCDName`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L5), and during training, random atomization can be applied with [`RandomAtomizeResidues`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L98). The pipeline also supports AlphaFold 3-like cropping strategies through [`CropContiguousLikeAF3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L62) and [`CropSpatialLikeAF3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L62). Changes introduced by cropping are tracked using [`annotate_pre_crop_hash`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py#L16) and [`annotate_post_crop_hash`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py#L22), with [`set_to_occupancy_0_where_crop_hashes_differ`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py#L28) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py) masking altered atoms. Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) for proteins and RNA are loaded, paired, merged, and featurized by components like [`LoadPolymerMSAs`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L95) and [`FeaturizeMSALikeAF3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L93). Token-level features are encoded by [`EncodeAF3TokenLevelFeatures`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/util_transforms.py#L366), while [`GetAF3ReferenceMoleculeFeatures`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L15) generates reference molecule features, often relying on RDKit for conformer generation. Chiral features are added by [`AddAF3ChiralFeatures`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L58), and bond features, including cyclic bonds detected by [`AddCyclicBonds`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/cyclic_transform.py#L9) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/cyclic_transform.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/cyclic_transform.py), are computed by [`AddAF3TokenBondFeatures`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L51). Diffusion-specific transforms, such as [`build_ground_truth_distogram_transform`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py#L45) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipeline_utils.py), prepare noised ground truth distograms for model conditioning. This transform, leveraging [`FeaturizeNoisedGroundTruthAsTemplateDistogram`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/ground_truth_template.py#L387) from [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/ground_truth_template.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/ground_truth_template.py), adds Gaussian noise to atomic coordinates and discretizes pairwise distances into a distogram. The pipeline also handles batching, augmentation, and noise sampling for diffusion models with [`BatchStructuresForDiffusionNoising`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L64) and [`SampleEDMNoise`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L66).

The model's ability to handle molecular data is supported by definitions of chemical properties and lookup tables in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/chemical.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/chemical.py), which includes [`aa2long`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/chemical.py#L16) for atom names and [`frames`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/chemical.py#L1276) for defining coordinate frames crucial for calculations such as FAPE (Frame Aligned Point Error).

Kinematic calculations are integral to RF3's understanding and manipulation of molecular structures. Functions in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/kinematics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/kinematics.py) perform essential operations like calculating pairwise distances ([`get_pair_dist`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/kinematics.py#L94)), angles ([`get_ang`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/kinematics.py#L112)), and dihedral angles ([`get_dih`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/kinematics.py#L135)). These utilities also convert 3D Cartesian coordinates to internal coordinate representations (e.g., [`xyz_to_c6d`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/kinematics.py#L181), [`xyz_to_t2d`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/kinematics.py#L231)), which are critical for structural modeling and sampling. Additionally, the system employs utilities for 3D coordinate alignment using [`weighted_rigid_align`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/utils/alignment.py#L8) and RMSD calculations with [`get_rmsd`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/utils/alignment.py#L87) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/alignment.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/alignment.py). These geometric tools ensure that the model can accurately represent and manipulate biomolecular structures during the prediction process.

### RF3 Loss Functions and Evaluation Metrics
Within RF3, various loss functions and evaluation metrics guide model training and assess prediction quality, including [`ConfidenceLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py#L18), [`DiffusionLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416), [`DistogramLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L628), lDDT scores, and specialized metrics for chirality and clashing. These components are primarily defined within the [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics) directories.

The [`DiffusionLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py) is central to the denoising diffusion process. It calculates the mean squared error between predicted and ground-truth coordinates, incorporating atom-specific weighting and optionally applying a smoothed lDDT loss. This loss is crucial for models that learn to reverse a diffusion process to generate structures. For evaluating clashing within predicted protein structures, the [`CountClashingChains`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/clashing_chains.py#L10) metric defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/clashing_chains.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/clashing_chains.py) identifies if a significant number of atoms from different chains are too close.

The [`DistogramLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L628) (found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py)) compares predicted inter-atomic distance distributions to ground-truth distributions using cross-entropy, guiding the model to learn correct spatial relationships between residues. Relatedly, various lDDT (Local Distance Difference Test) scores are employed for evaluating the accuracy of local atomic environments, with implementations such as [`AllAtomLDDT`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L205) and [`InterfaceLDDTByType`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L268) located in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py).

For predicting structural confidence, the [`ConfidenceLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py#L18) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py) combines several metrics: Predicted Local Distance Difference Test ([`plddt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L231)), Predicted Aligned Error ([`pae`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L231)), Predicted Distance Error ([`pde`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L300)), and expected resolved status ([`exp_resolved`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L391)). This loss treats confidence prediction as a classification problem over binned values, using cross-entropy. It also includes an optional ranking loss ([`listnet_loss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py#L511)) to prioritize the accuracy of confidence score ordering.

Chirality, a fundamental property in molecular structures, is evaluated by the [`ChiralLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py#L158) metric, detailed in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/chiral.py). This metric calculates the squared error of predicted dihedral angles against ideal angles for chiral centers and identifies the percentage of correctly predicted chiral centers. In addition, the system also incorporates analytical gradients for dihedral angle mean squared error loss with respect to atomic coordinates, primarily for chiral centers, as seen in [`calc_ddihedralmse_dxyz`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/loss.py#L8) within [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/loss.py). This approach is particularly useful when precise control over geometric constraints is required, potentially offering efficiency benefits over automatic differentiation.

Specialized losses for handling molecular symmetry are also present. [`ResidueSymmetryResolution`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L10) and [`SubunitSymmetryResolution`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L56) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py) aim to align predicted and native structures by finding optimal permutations or rigid transformations of symmetric elements, minimizing alignment metrics. These symmetry-aware losses ensure that models accurately capture and reproduce symmetrical molecular arrangements. For details on the overall RF3 model architecture, refer to [RF3 Model Architecture and Confidence Estimation](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rf3-model-architecture-and-confidence-estimation).

### RFD3 Diffusion Process and Input Specification
RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) employs a generative diffusion process for [`de novo`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L108) biomolecular design. The core of this process is managed by the [`RFD3DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L32) and the [`ConditionalDiffusionSampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L582), which work together to iteratively refine structures by removing noise.

The [`RFD3DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L32) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py) serves as the central neural network, taking noisy coordinates and other biomolecular features as input. It incorporates time-dependent features through Fourier embeddings and employs multiple attention mechanisms to process both atom-level and token-level representations. This module is capable of performing several passes, known as "recycling," where predictions from one pass are fed back as refined features to improve subsequent iterations. This iterative refinement allows the model to progressively denoise the input and predict more accurate atomic positions and sequence information.

The [`ConditionalDiffusionSampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L582) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py) orchestrates the iterative denoising steps. It applies the diffusion model in a controlled manner, managing the noise schedule and integrating various conditioning strategies. This sampler can handle specific design requirements such as fixed substructures (motifs) and symmetry. It supports applying classifier-free guidance to steer the design process more effectively. For detailed information on controlling the balance between designability and diversity in the generated outputs, refer to [Controlling Designability vs. Diversity](#rfdiffusion3-rfd3-for-de-novo-design-rfd3-inference-and-design-examples-controlling-designability-vs-diversity).

Users control the design process through an [`InputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L112), defined in JSON or YAML files, as detailed in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md). This specification allows for precise definition of design constraints:

*   **[`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) regions**: These strings define indexed motif specifications, indicating which parts of the input structure should be fixed, designed, or left as chain breaks. For example, a contig can specify residues from an input structure (e.g., "A1-80") or define a desired length for a newly designed region (e.g., "70-80"). RFD3NA extends this concept to multipolymer contigs, as explained in [RFD3NA Multipolymer Contig Specification and Input Selection](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3na-multipolymer-contig-specification-and-input-selection).
*   **[`ligand`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L142) specification**: Users can specify small molecules by their chemical component name or index, allowing for the design of protein-ligand interactions.
*   **Selection methods**: A flexible mini-language, [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26), enables precise specification of residues and atoms for various conditioning types. This includes:
    *   [`select_fixed_atoms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L152): To fix coordinates of specific atoms or regions.
    *   [`select_unfixed_sequence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L160): To define regions where the amino acid sequence can be redesigned.
    *   [`select_buried`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L170), [`select_exposed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L172): For conditioning based on solvent accessibility (RASA).
    *   [`select_hbond_donor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L175), [`select_hbond_acceptor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L174): For atom-wise hydrogen bond conditioning, guiding the model to form specific hydrogen bonds.
    *   [`select_hotspots`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L176): To designate specific atoms or residues as critical interaction points.
*   **[`partial_t`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L193)**: This parameter enables "partial diffusion" by introducing a specific noise level to the sampler. This is useful for refining existing structures or designing around a pre-defined scaffold.

The [`RFD3InferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L140) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py) orchestrates the entire inference process by canonicalizing inputs, batching design specifications, and managing outputs. This engine also supports optional [`torch.compile`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L227) optimization for performance, and can save trajectory files for debugging and analysis.

### RFD3 Training and Advanced Conditioning
RFD3's training methodology employs a robust framework leveraging [`hydra`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L27) for flexible configuration and [`lightning.fabric`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L84) for scalable distributed training. The core training execution is managed by the [`train`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py#L26) function in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/train.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/train.py), which orchestrates the entire lifecycle, from loading configurations and setting up the environment to instantiating models, optimizers, and schedulers. This setup also handles distributed data loading, ensuring efficient data distribution across multiple training processes.

Central to RFD3's training is the [`AADesignTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33) class, found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py). This class specializes in protein design-specific training logic, including the preparation of network inputs, calculation of the total loss, and evaluation of various design metrics during validation. It uses a [`recycle_schedule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L65) to determine the number of recycling steps for each training batch, which is crucial for iterative refinement of structural predictions. Furthermore, the trainer incorporates a [`DumpValidationStructuresCallback`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/dump_validation_structures.py#L19) to save predicted structures and associated metadata during validation, facilitating detailed analysis of training progress.

A key aspect of RFD3's training involves sophisticated conditioning strategies designed to create diverse and challenging design problems. These strategies are implemented using a class-based system defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py). The [`TrainingCondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L31) abstract base class provides a common interface for different conditioning approaches. Concrete implementations like [`IslandCondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L56) allow for selecting "islands" of residues as motifs, controlling which atoms or tokens are fixed in terms of coordinates or sequence. [`PPICondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L176), on the other hand, is tailored for protein-protein interaction training, defining motifs based on binder and target proteins to fix the target's sequence and coordinates. [`SubtypeCondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L272) focuses on selecting specific atom subtypes (e.g., protein, ligand, DNA) as motifs for conditioning. These conditions dynamically set conditioning annotations on [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects (e.g., [`is_motif_atom_with_fixed_coord`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L10), [`is_motif_atom_with_fixed_seq`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L9), [`is_motif_atom_unindexed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L11)), allowing the model to learn to generate structures under various constraints.

The application of these conditioning strategies is managed by transforms within [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py). [`SampleConditioningType`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L213) and [`SampleConditioningFlags`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L292) are used during training to probabilistically select and apply different conditioning strategies, while [`UnindexFlaggedTokens`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L315) handles the expansion of unindexed motifs, a critical step for preventing positional leakage in relative positional encoding when dealing with designed regions. These mechanisms collectively enable RFD3 to be trained on a wide array of design problems, improving its ability to generate novel biomolecular structures under diverse design specifications.

### RFD3NA Multipolymer Contig Specification and Input Selection
RFD3NA introduces a flexible [`InputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L112) for defining complex multipolymer designs, enabling users to precisely control the design process from initial input structures to conditioning constraints. The core of this specification is the [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) mini-language, which extends beyond protein design to encompass nucleic acids. For instance, [`10-10,20-20R,30-30D`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/README.md#L55) specifies a design with a 10-residue protein segment, a 20-residue RNA segment, and a 30-residue DNA segment. This syntax allows for the definition of fixed and designed regions, chain breaks, and the explicit typing of polymer chains as protein, RNA, or DNA. Beyond [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) definition, the [`InputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L112) manages various other parameters such as [`unindex`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L135) for motif tokens with unknown relative sequence placement, [`length`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L141) constraints for designed regions, and [`ligand`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L142) specification for small molecule interactions.

The [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) mini-language, detailed in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/input.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/input.md), provides a unified way to specify residue and atom selections across different fields within the [`InputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L112). This powerful selection mechanism supports boolean values, contig-style strings, and dictionaries, with shorthand values like [`ALL`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L148), [`TIP`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L77), and [`BKBN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/README.md#L90) for common selections. It is crucial for defining constraints such as [`select_fixed_atoms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L152) (atoms with fixed coordinates), [`select_unfixed_sequence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L160) (regions where sequence can change), and various conditioning features like [`select_buried`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L170), [`select_exposed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L172) for solvent accessibility, and [`select_hbond_donor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L175), [`select_hbond_acceptor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L174) for hydrogen bond specific conditioning.

Beyond basic structural definitions, RFD3NA's input system also supports advanced constraints essential for nucleic acid design. This includes specifying RNA secondary structure using dot-bracket notation, either globally via [`ss_dbn`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L48) or for specific regions via [`ss_dbn_dict`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L65). Furthermore, fine-grained control over base-pairing is achieved through [`paired_region_list`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L91), [`loop_region_list`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L92), and [`paired_position_list`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L116). The [`DesignInputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L115) class, primarily defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/input_parsing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/input_parsing.py), parses and validates these user-defined parameters, translating them into an [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) annotated with relevant features for the downstream diffusion model. This process involves a [`build`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L88) method that orchestrates the construction of the final [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20), including steps like deep copying and reordering atoms, appending ligands, applying symmetry transformations, and setting the origin token. This comprehensive input system, including support for legacy formats via [`LegacySpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L80), ensures robust and flexible control over multipolymer design. For more details on the transformation capabilities and symmetry operations, refer to [RFD3NA Data Transforms and Symmetry Operations](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3na-data-transforms-and-symmetry-operations).

### RFD3NA Data Transforms and Symmetry Operations
The RFD3NA framework leverages a comprehensive suite of data transformations to prepare molecular structures for multipolymer design, ensuring accurate representation and conditioning. These transformations are critical for tasks ranging from conditioning the diffusion process to generating specialized features and applying symmetry constraints.

A core aspect of this framework is the definition and application of various **conditioning strategies**. These strategies, implemented as [`Transform`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L453) classes, guide the model by specifying fixed regions, motifs, or designable areas within a molecular structure. Files such as [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/conditioning_base.py) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/training_conditions.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/training_conditions.py) manage the global conditioning syntax. This includes [`IslandCondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L56) for selecting token "islands" as motifs, [`PPICondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L176) for defining protein-protein interaction interfaces, and [`SubtypeCondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L272) for targeting specific molecular subtypes like protein, DNA, or RNA. These conditions dictate how annotations such as [`is_motif_atom_with_fixed_seq`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L9) (fixed sequence), [`is_motif_atom_with_fixed_coord`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L10) (fixed coordinates), and [`is_motif_atom_unindexed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L11) (tokens whose positions are diffused) are applied to the [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20). The [`UnindexFlaggedTokens`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L315) transform is particularly significant as it handles the expansion of unindexed motifs and generates [`unindexing_pair_mask`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L341) for relative positional encoding, ensuring proper information flow within the model.

**Feature generation** is another critical component, detailed within [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/design_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/design_transforms.py). These transforms create diverse molecular features essential for the model's predictive capabilities. Examples include [`CreateDesignReferenceFeatures`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L117) for generating reference positions and motif token classes, [`FeaturizeAtoms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L346) for adding atom-wise properties like RASA and hydrogen bond donor/acceptor states, and [`AddIsXFeats`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L399) for boolean masks indicating atom types (e.g., backbone, alpha carbon). Noise augmentation, such as [`AugmentNoise`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py#L611), is also applied here to enhance the robustness of diffusion models during training.

The framework incorporates specialized transformations for **hydrogen bond calculations**. [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/hbonds.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/hbonds.py) handles the addition of hydrogen atoms and the calculation of hydrogen bonds using [`biotite`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/.env#L19), while [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py) integrates with the external [`HBPLUS`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L143) tool for more sophisticated H-bond analysis. These transforms annotate structures with [`active_donor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L85) and [`active_acceptor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L85) features, which are vital for designing hydrogen bond-mediated interactions.

A key capability for multipolymer design is the handling of **nucleic acid secondary structure**. The [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/na_geom.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/na_geom.py) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/na_geom_utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/na_geom_utils.py) modules compute nucleic acid secondary structure features, including base-pair partners and counts, either from geometric analysis or user-provided specifications like dot-bracket strings. This allows the model to explicitly condition on or generate desired nucleic acid conformations.

**Symmetry operations** are crucial for designing symmetric biomolecular assemblies, and are primarily managed by [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/symmetry.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/symmetry.py). The [`AddSymmetryFeats`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py#L10) transform extracts and integrates symmetry-related transformations ([`sym_transform`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py#L33)) and annotations ([`sym_transform_id`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py#L22), [`sym_entity_id`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py#L23), [`is_sym_asu`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/symmetry.py#L24)) into the data. These features help ensure that generated structures adhere to specified symmetries, maintaining structural integrity across repeated units. Further details on symmetry handling in RFD3NA, including utility functions like [`add_sym_annotations`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/symmetry/atom_array.py#L15) and [`apply_symmetry_to_atomarray_coord`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/symmetry/atom_array.py#L152), can be found in [RFD3NA Multipolymer Contig Specification and Input Selection](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3na-multipolymer-contig-specification-and-input-selection) and [RFD3NA Input Specification and Multipolymer Contigs](#rfdiffusion3na-rfd3na-for-multipolymer-design-rfd3na-input-specification-and-multipolymer-contigs). The tests in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/tests`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/tests) validate these symmetry operations, confirming that atoms are correctly assigned to symmetry mates and that the structural relationships are preserved.

The orchestration of these diverse transformations into coherent pipelines is handled by [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/pipelines.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/pipelines.py). This module uses constructs like [`Compose`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/utils/rigid.py#L626) to sequence transforms, [`ConditionalRoute`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L42) for executing transforms based on specific conditions (e.g., training vs. inference), and [`RandomRoute`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L45) for stochastic elements like cropping. This modular design enables flexible and powerful data preparation workflows tailored to various multipolymer design challenges.

## Protein and Ligand Inverse Folding (MPNN)
The Message Passing Neural Network (MPNN) models, including ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, and SolubleMPNN, provide functionalities for protein and ligand sequence design given a fixed backbone structure. These models are re-implemented within the Foundry framework, leveraging [`atomworks`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/.env#L12) and [`foundry`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L95) for backend support, aiming for stability and performance. The architecture for these models typically involves graph featurization, message passing layers, and specific decoding strategies for sequence generation.

The data preparation pipelines handle the conversion of raw structural data into features suitable for model input. This involves cleaning and filtering structural components, atomization, indexing, and generating residue- and atom-level features. The pipelines also integrate user-defined settings, such as structural noise or causality patterns, and compute polymer-ligand interface masks when applicable.

Training infrastructure for MPNN models utilizes a token-budgeted batching system and efficient collators to manage variable-length examples. The training process uses a [`LabelSmoothedNLLLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py#L7) for optimizing model parameters and [`NoamOpt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L49)-style learning rate schedulers. The [`MPNNTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21) orchestrates the training and validation loops, including model construction and metric computation.

For inference, the [`MPNNInferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) manages model loading, processing input structures through the data transformation pipeline, and decoding sequences. This engine supports loading legacy model weights from original implementations. Evaluation metrics such as negative log-likelihood (NLL), perplexity, confidence scores, and sequence recovery are computed to assess design quality, both generally and for specific interface residues. Output structures and FASTA files are generated as part of the inference process. For more information on MPNN model architecture and core functionality, see [MPNN Model Architecture and Core Functionality](#protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-mpnn-model-architecture-and-core-functionality). Data preparation and transformation pipelines are detailed in [MPNN Data Preparation and Transformation Pipelines](#protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-mpnn-data-preparation-and-transformation-pipelines), while the training infrastructure and loss functions are covered in [MPNN Training Infrastructure and Loss Functions](#protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-mpnn-training-infrastructure-and-loss-functions). The inference engine and evaluation metrics are further discussed in [MPNN Inference Engine and Evaluation Metrics](#protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-mpnn-inference-engine-and-evaluation-metrics).

### MPNN Model Architecture and Core Functionality
The Foundry [`ProteinMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21), [`LigandMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2303), and [`SolubleMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2173) models employ a graph neural network architecture to design biomolecular sequences based on three-dimensional structural information. The core functionality, primarily embodied by the [`ProteinMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) class located in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py), centers on representing biological structures as graphs, processing these graphs through message passing, and then decoding them into amino acid or ligand sequences.

This architecture begins with **graph featurization**, where input structures are converted into numerical representations suitable for the neural network. This involves extracting a variety of features, including 3D coordinates of atoms, pairwise distances between residues or atoms, and radial basis function (RBF) embeddings that capture geometric relationships. These featurization methods are primarily defined in modules like [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py). Specialized feature extraction caters to different scenarios, such as incorporating membrane information, Position-Specific Scoring Matrix (PSSM) data, or detailed protein-ligand interaction features, by extending the base [`ProteinFeatures`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/graph_embeddings.py#L11) class.

Following featurization, **message passing layers** propagate information across the graph. These layers, implemented as [`EncLayer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L114) (encoder) and [`DecLayer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py#L227) (decoder) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/message_passing.py), iteratively update the hidden states of both nodes (representing residues or atoms) and edges (representing interactions between them). These updates are facilitated by helper functions that gather and concatenate features from neighboring nodes and edges, allowing the model to integrate local structural context. Nonlinear transformations within these layers are typically performed by [`PositionWiseFeedForward`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/position_wise_feed_forward.py#L5) networks, defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/position_wise_feed_forward.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/position_wise_feed_forward.py).

**Positional encoding** is crucial for providing the model with information about the relative positions of residues within and between polymer chains. The [`PositionalEncodings`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py#L5) class in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/layers/positional_encoding.py) generates learned embeddings from pairwise residue offsets and chain identity masks. This enables the model to distinguish between interactions within the same chain versus those between different chains, a fundamental aspect of biomolecular structure.

Finally, the models employ **decoding strategies** to predict sequences. During training, a "teacher-forcing" approach can be used, where the model is guided by the true sequence. For inference, an "autoregressive" decoding strategy is often employed, where residues are predicted iteratively, building the sequence one by one. The [`ProteinMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) class orchestrates these steps, including managing causality masks that control the flow of information during the decoding process and converting raw model outputs into sampled sequences. The inference engine then handles loading these models and applying them to new structural inputs. See [MPNN Inference Engine and Evaluation Metrics](#protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-mpnn-inference-engine-and-evaluation-metrics) for more details.

### MPNN Data Preparation and Transformation Pipelines
The data preparation and transformation pipelines for MPNN models convert raw structural data into a feature set suitable for model input, encompassing cleaning, atomization, featurization of user settings, and calculations for polymer-ligand interfaces. These pipelines are primarily defined and configured within the [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines) directory, where the [`build_mpnn_transform_pipeline`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py#L61) function constructs a [`Compose`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/utils/rigid.py#L626) object.
