This object orchestrates a series of transformations for both training and inference scenarios, adapting based on configuration parameters such as [`model_type`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L26) (protein or ligand MPNN), [`occupancy_threshold`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py#L139), and [`is_inference`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/testing/debug.py#L38).

The process begins with structural cleaning, which includes removing hydrogen atoms and handling undesired residues or non-clashing chains during training. The system then performs atomization and residue processing, adding within-chain residue indices, managing covalent modifications, and flagging non-polymeric components for atomization. For example, the [`AtomizeByCCDName`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L5) transform in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py) atomizes components that are not standard or unknown amino acids. Occupancy-based filtering masks and removes residues where backbone atoms fall below a specified occupancy threshold, ensuring data quality.

Feature encoding and featurization steps follow, where [`EncodeMPNNNonAtomizedTokens`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py#L14) generates core MPNN features like coordinates ([`X`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L144)), atom masks ([`X_m`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L1955)), and sequence encodings ([`S`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L161)) for residue-level tokens. [`FeaturizeNonAtomizedTokens`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py#L89) adds residue-level features such as [`R_idx`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L1959) (residue indices) and [`chain_labels`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L1960). For atomized tokens, [`FeaturizeAtomizedTokens`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py#L144) generates atomic coordinates ([`Y`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/docs/examples/9dfn.cif#L80)), atomic numbers ([`Y_t`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2628)), and masks ([`Y_m`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2626)) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/mpnn.py).

A key aspect of data preparation involves defining token and atom orderings, handled by [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/token_encodings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/token_encodings.py). This ensures consistent representation of amino acid tokens and their constituent atoms for feature aggregation, providing both current and legacy orderings for compatibility.

User-defined settings are integrated via [`FeaturizeUserSettings`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py#L21) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/user_settings.py). This transform processes scalar settings like [`structure_noise`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L1995) (for data augmentation during training) and [`decode_type`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L1998), as well as array-wide settings such as [`mpnn_designed_residue_mask`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py#L700) and [`mpnn_temperature`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py#L701). It also handles the conversion of sparse [`mpnn_pair_bias`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/README.md#L140) into a dense matrix for token-level interactions.

For scenarios involving interactions, [`ComputePolymerLigandInterface`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py#L17) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/polymer_ligand_interface.py) identifies and annotates atoms at the polymer-ligand interface based on a distance threshold. This information is then used by [`FeaturizePolymerLigandInterfaceMask`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py#L16) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/transforms/feature_aggregation/polymer_ligand_interface.py) to create a residue-level mask, indicating which polymer residues are in contact with a ligand.

Finally, the pipeline converts the processed features into [`torch.Tensor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/common.py#L106) objects and ensures that only the required [`input_features`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L174) and [`atom_array`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L93) are returned, making the data ready for the MPNN model. The conditional routing and modular design, facilitated by [`ConditionalRoute`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py#L42) objects in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/pipelines/mpnn.py), allow for flexible and extensible data preparation workflows tailored to different model types and operational modes. For further details on the MPNN model architecture, see [Protein and Ligand Inverse Folding (MPNN) Architecture and Core Functionality](#introduction-to-foundry-models-protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-architecture-and-core-functionality).

### MPNN Training Infrastructure and Loss Functions
The training infrastructure for MPNN models centers around efficient data handling, distributed learning, and a specialized loss function. The training process, orchestrated by the [`MPNNTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21), utilizes token-budgeted batching and sophisticated data collators to optimize GPU memory usage and computational efficiency.

Data handling begins with [`PaddedTokenBudgetBatchSampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py#L9) (defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/samplers/samplers.py) and further detailed in [MPNN Data Preparation and Transformation Pipelines](#protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-mpnn-data-preparation-and-transformation-pipelines)). This sampler ensures that batches are constructed with a token budget in mind, minimizing padding by grouping samples of similar lengths. This is achieved by sorting samples by their token counts and then greedily forming batches that adhere to a [`max_tokens_with_padding`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L211) limit. The sampler also provides an epoch-based caching mechanism to optimize batch generation. Complementing this, [`TokenBudgetAwareFeatureCollator`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py#L187) (found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/collate/feature_collator.py)) handles the actual batch collation, managing variable-length features through padding and ensuring consistency of scalar features across the batch. It filters examples to ensure that the token budget is met, dropping larger examples if necessary.

The core training logic resides within the [`MPNNTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21) class (located at [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py) and elaborated in [MPNN Model Architecture and Core Functionality](#protein-and-ligand-inverse-folding-mpnn-mpnn-model-architecture-and-core-functionality)). This trainer, built upon PyTorch Lightning Fabric, manages the entire training and validation lifecycle. It constructs either [`ProteinMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) or [`LigandMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2303) models and employs a [`LabelSmoothedNLLLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py#L7) (see [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/loss/nll_loss.py)) as its fixed loss function. This loss function incorporates label smoothing to prevent overconfidence in predictions and normalizes the aggregated loss by a constant value. The [`MPNNTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/trainers/mpnn.py#L21) also handles distributed training effectively by leveraging [`fabric.no_backward_sync`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L230) for gradient accumulation during distributed data parallel (DDP) setups, enhancing scalability. The training flow includes a Noam-style learning rate scheduler to dynamically adjust the learning rate during different training phases, and robust checkpointing mechanisms for saving and restoring model states (for more details on general training infrastructure, see [Training Harness with PyTorch Lightning Fabric](#foundry-core-library-and-ml-workflows-training-harness-with-pytorch-lightning-fabric)).

### MPNN Inference Engine and Evaluation Metrics
The MPNN inference engine orchestrates the entire process of sequence design using ProteinMPNN and LigandMPNN models. The core component, the [`MPNNInferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) class located in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py), is responsible for initializing the engine, configuring model parameters and output settings, and managing the execution of inference runs. It validates configurations such as [`model_type`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/train.py#L26), [`checkpoint_path`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference.py#L31), and [`out_directory`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L176) to ensure proper setup.

Model loading is a key function, where [`MPNNInferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) builds and loads the appropriate [`ProteinMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L21) or [`LigandMPNN`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/model/mpnn.py#L2303) model. It supports both standard and legacy checkpoint formats, with older weights undergoing a series of transformations to adapt to the current model implementation. These transformations, handled by [`load_legacy_weights`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py#L20) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/weights.py), involve renaming parameters, adjusting atom type embeddings, and reordering backbone distance and amino acid token embeddings to ensure compatibility. The system also handles the detection of available hardware accelerators (CUDA, XPU, MPS), falling back to CPU if none are present to ensure broad compatibility.

During inference, the [`MPNNInferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/inference_engines/mpnn.py#L38) processes input structures, batching them and applying a transformation pipeline to convert raw structural data into features suitable for the model. After the model's forward pass, predicted sequences are decoded from the model's output. The designed sequences, along with per-residue confidence scores, are then used to update the input [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects. Side-chain atoms that are no longer relevant to the redesigned sequence are removed, retaining only backbone and fixed atoms.

Evaluation metrics provide crucial insights into the model's performance and the quality of designed sequences. The metrics are defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics) and include:
*   **Negative Log Likelihood (NLL)** and **Perplexity**: The [`NLL`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L14) class in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py) calculates these metrics based on ground truth sequences and predicted log probabilities. Specialized versions like [`InterfaceNLL`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L222) compute these specifically for residues at the polymer-ligand interface, identified dynamically using distance thresholds and atom arrays.
*   **Confidence Scores**: [`MPNNConfidence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L495) and [`MPNNLigandInterfaceConfidence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/nll.py#L539) derive confidence scores from sampled sequence NLL, indicating the model's certainty in its predictions, both generally and for interface residues.
*   **Sequence Recovery**: The [`SequenceRecovery`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py#L14) class in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py) measures the percentage of correctly predicted residues by comparing sampled and argmax sequences against ground truth. [`InterfaceSequenceRecovery`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/metrics/sequence_recovery.py#L294) extends this to evaluate recovery specifically within protein-ligand interface regions.

The CLI utilities in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py) provide a user-friendly interface for initiating inference runs. They manage argument parsing, JSON configuration loading, and the creation of structured [`MPNNInferenceInput`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py#L681) objects. These objects encapsulate [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) data along with inference parameters, including detailed specifications for design scope (e.g., fixed or designed residues/chains), bias settings, temperature, and symmetry constraints. After inference, results are stored in [`MPNNInferenceOutput`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/src/mpnn/utils/inference.py#L2206) objects, which can then be used to write designed structures as CIF files and sequences as FASTA files, complete with metadata. The system ensures robust error handling and configuration validation throughout the process.

## RoseTTAFold3 (RF3) for Structure Prediction
RoseTTAFold3 (RF3) is a biomolecular structure prediction model designed to determine the 3D atomic coordinates of proteins and other biomolecules. It supports a wide range of inputs, including sequences, multiple sequence alignments (MSAs), small molecules, DNA, and RNA, and can handle covalent modifications and complex topologies.

Users can install RF3 and download model checkpoints, including [`Latest`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L39), [`Preprint`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L40), and [`Benchmark`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L41) versions. The model supports inference for various biomolecular systems. Predictions are executed via a command-line interface, which allows specifying inputs, output directories, and checkpoint paths. Input formats are versatile, accommodating JSON, CIF, PDB, SMILES, and SDF files. For efficient processing, RF3 supports batching multiple inputs, automatically distributing jobs across available GPUs.

Beyond basic prediction, RF3 incorporates advanced features for controlling the folding process. Templating capabilities enable guiding predictions using known structural elements, applicable to both polymers and non-polymers. Users can specify [`template_selection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L68) for token-level guidance and [`ground_truth_conformer_selection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/inference.py#L69) to enforce specific residue conformations, particularly useful for small molecules. Performance parameters like [`early_stopping_plddt_threshold`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L138), [`n_recycles`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L582), [`diffusion_batch_size`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L48), [`num_steps`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L586), and [`seed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L81) can be configured to optimize computational resources and prediction quality. The model provides comprehensive outputs, including confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE), [`.cif`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L119) structure files, and options to dump trajectories or annotate B-factors with pLDDT values.

The RF3 model's architecture is centered around a [`FeatureInitializer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/pairformer_layers.py#L401), [`Recycler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L257), [`DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L70), and [`DistogramHead`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L233) (defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py)). The [`DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3_structure.py#L70) manages the iterative denoising process during training and diffusion rollouts during inference, guided by an [`inference_sampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54). For enhanced confidence estimation, [`RF3WithConfidence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/RF3.py#L334) extends the base model by incorporating a [`ConfidenceHead`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py#L25) (from [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/model/layers/af3_auxiliary_heads.py)) to predict [`pLDDT`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L231) and [`PAE`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L231) metrics, which can be used for early stopping to save computational time.

Training and validation workflows for RF3 are orchestrated by specialized trainers (e.g., [`RF3Trainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L35) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py)), which handle loss calculation, metric evaluation, and molecular symmetry resolution. Data preparation involves sophisticated pipelines that process raw structural data and generate features suitable for model input. These pipelines include transformations for handling cyclic bonds, generating noised ground truth distogram features, and assembling AF3-like data processing streams (see [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data/pipelines.py) and other modules within [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/data)).

RF3 leverages a comprehensive suite of loss functions and evaluation metrics to guide training and assess prediction quality. Loss functions such as [`ConfidenceLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py#L18), [`DiffusionLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416), and [`DistogramLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L628) (found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_confidence_loss.py) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py)) are critical for model optimization. Evaluation metrics cover various aspects of structural accuracy, including chirality, atom clashing, lDDT scores (e.g., [`AllAtomLDDT`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L205), [`InterfaceLDDTByType`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/lddt.py#L268)), and predicted error metrics ([`ComputePTM`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/predicted_error.py#L43), [`ComputeIPTM`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics/predicted_error.py#L73)) located within submodules of [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/metrics). These metrics help ensure that the generated structures are chemically plausible and structurally accurate.

For further details on the RF3 model's architectural components and confidence estimation, refer to [RF3 Model Architecture and Confidence Estimation](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rf3-model-architecture-and-confidence-estimation). For in-depth information on data processing and kinematic calculations, see [RF3 Advanced Data Processing and Kinematics](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rf3-advanced-data-processing-and-kinematics). The specific loss functions and evaluation metrics are discussed in [RF3 Loss Functions and Evaluation Metrics](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rf3-loss-functions-and-evaluation-metrics).

## RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) for De Novo Design
RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) is a diffusion-based model for *de novo* biomolecular interaction design, capable of generating novel proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules. It supports various design tasks such as sequence prediction, inverse folding, and sidechain design.

To get started with RFD3, installation typically involves [`pip install rc-foundry[rfd3]`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L143) and downloading model checkpoints using [`foundry install rfd3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L1). A key advanced feature for biomolecular design is hydrogen bond conditioning, which requires a separate installation of [`HBPLUS`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L143) and updating its path in the Foundry environment file. Detailed installation instructions are available in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/tutorials/RFdiffusion3_installation_tutorial.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/tutorials/RFdiffusion3_installation_tutorial.md).

Inference with RFD3 is performed using the [`rfd3 design`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L1) command, which takes an output directory and an [`inputs`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L102) JSON/YAML file specifying design constraints. The [`RFD3InferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L140) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py) handles input processing, batching, and output generation. The core diffusion process is managed by the [`RFD3DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L32) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py) and the [`ConditionalDiffusionSampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L582) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py), which iteratively denoises structures with conditional diffusion and classifier-free guidance. Output structures are saved as [`.cif.gz`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L620) files, with design metrics in accompanying [`.json`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L67) files. For detailed examples, including enzyme design, nucleic acid binder design, and protein binder design, refer to the [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples) directory. Users can also control the trade-off between designability and diversity in generated outputs using parameters like [`inference_sampler.step_scale`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L69) and [`inference_sampler.gamma_0`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/designability_vs_diversity.md#L8), or by setting [`is_non_loopy`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L191) in the input configuration, as discussed in [Controlling Designability vs. Diversity](#rfdiffusion3-rfd3-for-de-novo-design-rfd3-inference-and-design-examples-controlling-designability-vs-diversity).

The training infrastructure for RFD3 is built on [`lightning.fabric`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L84) for distributed training and leverages Hydra for configuration management. The [`AADesignTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py) implements the protein design-specific training logic. A key aspect of RFD3 training is its sophisticated conditioning strategy, which creates random design problems by fixing atoms, sequences, or coordinates. This is primarily controlled via [`training_conditions`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L171) within the configuration files, as detailed in [RFD3 Training and Advanced Conditioning](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3-training-and-advanced-conditioning). The system supports logging with Weights & Biases or CSV for tracking training progress. The framework also includes various [`Transform`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L453) classes for preparing [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) data, managing conditioning, generating design features, and calculating hydrogen bonds, which are crucial for guiding the model during both training and inference. These are located within [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms).

### RFD3 Input Specification and Conditioning
RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) utilizes a structured approach to input specification, primarily through JSON or YAML files, allowing users to define precise constraints for *de novo* biomolecular design tasks. This system enables detailed control over the design process, from specifying fixed structural elements to guiding the generation of new sequences and conformations. The core of this system is the [`InputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L112), which is managed and validated by the [`DesignInputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L115) Pydantic model found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py).

Users define design problems by providing a base structure (a PDB or CIF file) and then layering constraints. Key among these constraints is the [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) string, which specifies regions of the molecule that are fixed, designable, or represent chain breaks. For instance, a [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) like [`"A1-80,10,/0,B5-12"`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L125) would fix residues 1-80 of chain A, specify a designable segment of 10 residues, introduce a chain break, and fix residues 5-12 of chain B. This mini-language allows for fine-grained control over the topological arrangement of the designed molecule. For cases where the relative sequence placement of a motif is unknown, [`unindex`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L135) tokens can be used, with the condition that at least one atom within an unindexed residue must be fixed to provide an anchor. The overall [`length`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L141) of the designed molecule can also be constrained.

Beyond defining the backbone, RFD3 allows for explicit specification of [`ligand`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L142) molecules by name or index. To further guide the design, various selection methods are available using the [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) mini-language. This flexible language allows for the designation of specific atoms or residues for different types of conditioning. For example, [`select_fixed_atoms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L152) can be used to anchor portions of the input structure, ensuring their coordinates remain unchanged during diffusion. Other selectors, such as [`select_unfixed_sequence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L160), define regions where the amino acid sequence can vary. Conditioning related to solvent accessibility can be applied using [`select_buried`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L170), [`select_partially_buried`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L171), or [`select_exposed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L172) to favor designs with specific exposure characteristics for certain residues. Hotspots, important for directing interaction interfaces, can be specified using [`select_hotspots`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L176) at either the atom or residue level.

A crucial aspect of biomolecular design, particularly for protein-ligand or protein-nucleic acid interactions, is hydrogen bond conditioning. RFD3 provides [`select_hbond_donor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L175) and [`select_hbond_acceptor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L174) to specify atoms that should act as hydrogen bond donors or acceptors, respectively. This allows the model to generate designs that satisfy specific hydrogen bonding networks, which are fundamental to molecular recognition and stability. The internal mechanisms for hydrogen bond calculations are defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py).

The [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) mini-language itself is highly adaptable, accepting boolean values, contig-style strings, or dictionaries to define selections for residues and atoms. This standardization ensures a consistent way to specify conditions across different design parameters. During inference, these input specifications are processed by the [`RFD3InferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L140) as detailed in [RFD3 Diffusion Process and Input Specification](#introduction-to-foundry-models-rfd3-diffusion-process-and-input-specification), which canonicalizes inputs and prepares them for the diffusion process.

Finally, [`partial_t`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L193) enables a technique called partial diffusion. By setting a specific noise level, this parameter allows the model to start designing from a partially diffused structure rather than from pure noise. This feature is particularly useful for scaffolding or refining existing structures, as it provides a way to incorporate an initial structural bias into the generative process. The implementation of input parsing and [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) preparation, including handling of legacy input formats and symmetry operations, is comprehensively managed within the [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference) directory. The [`create_atom_array_from_design_specification_legacy`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/legacy_input_parsing.py#L637) function in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/legacy_input_parsing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/legacy_input_parsing.py) ensures backward compatibility for older design configurations.

### RFD3 Inference and Design Examples
The RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) inference process orchestrates the *de novo* design of biomolecules through iterative denoising, producing novel structures based on specified constraints. The primary entry point for inference is [`rfd3 design`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L1), which can be executed from the command line after installation or by directly running the script in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/run_inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/run_inference.py). This process is managed by the [`RFD3InferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L140) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py), which handles input parsing, batching, and output generation.

Users define design problems using an [`InputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L112) (detailed in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md)), which can be provided via JSON or YAML files. This specification allows for precise control over design constraints, such as defining fixed and designable regions using [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) strings (e.g., [`"A1-10,/0,B15-24,/0,120-130"`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/demo.json#L32) for protein, DNA, and RNA chains), specifying ligands, fixing atom coordinates using [`select_fixed_atoms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L152), or applying hydrogen bond conditioning with [`select_hbond_donor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L175) and [`select_hbond_acceptor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L174). The [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) mini-language provides a flexible way to select specific residues and atoms for these constraints.

The core of the inference process involves the [`ConditionalDiffusionSampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L582) (found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py)), which performs iterative sampling and denoising. This sampler can operate with conditional diffusion and classifier-free guidance, enabling fine-grained control over the generated designs. The process also supports partial diffusion, where design occurs around already partially diffused structures, enabled by the [`partial_t`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L193) parameter.

RFD3 supports a wide array of design examples, showcasing its versatility across different biomolecular systems. These include:
*   **Enzyme Design:** Configuring enzyme design tasks by specifying input theozymes, identifying ligands, and defining fixed catalytic residues (illustrated in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/enzyme_design.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/enzyme_design.md)).
*   **Nucleic Acid Binder Design:** Designing proteins that bind to dsDNA, ssDNA, or RNA, involving complex [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) specifications, length definitions, and hydrogen bond conditioning (examples in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/na_binder_design.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/na_binder_design.md)).
*   **Protein Binder Design:** Creating novel protein-protein interfaces by defining target proteins, binder lengths, and binding hotspots. This often involves adjusting parameters like [`inference_sampler.step_scale`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L69) and [`inference_sampler.gamma_0`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/designability_vs_diversity.md#L8) to balance designability and diversity (detailed in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/protein_binder_design.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/protein_binder_design.md)). Further discussion on balancing designability and diversity is available in [Controlling Designability vs. Diversity](#rfdiffusion3-rfd3-for-de-novo-design-rfd3-inference-and-design-examples-controlling-designability-vs-diversity).
*   **Small Molecule Binder Design:** Designing proteins to encapsulate or interact with specific small molecules, using [`select_fixed_atoms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L152), [`select_exposed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L172), and [`select_buried`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L170) to guide the placement and interaction of the protein with the ligand (see [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/sm_binder_design.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/sm_binder_design.md)).
*   **Symmetry Design:** Generating proteins with precise cyclic ([`C`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L61)) or dihedral ([`D`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L392)) symmetries, either unconditionally or by scaffolding around existing motifs. The [`symmetry`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L185) object in the input JSON/YAML allows defining the symmetry group and identifying motifs that should or should not be symmetrized (explained in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/symmetry.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/symmetry.md)).

After successful inference, RFD3 outputs generated structures as [`.cif.gz`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L620) files and design metrics as [`.json`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L67) files, providing comprehensive results for analysis. The utility script [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/run_inf_tutorial.sh`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/run_inf_tutorial.sh) demonstrates how to orchestrate multiple inference runs and manage output files.

#### Controlling Designability vs. Diversity
RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) offers mechanisms to fine-tune the balance between generating highly designable (i.e., structurally stable and functional) biomolecules and exploring a broader range of diverse (i.e., varied structural motifs) designs. This trade-off is critical for various protein design applications, where either highly optimized solutions or novel scaffolds may be prioritized. The primary controls for this balance are implemented through inference parameters and input specifications.

One method for adjusting this balance is through **low-temperature sampling**, controlled by parameters in the inference sampler. The [`inference_sampler.step_scale`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L69) parameter, with a default of [`1.5`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L69), influences the step size during the diffusion process. Increasing this value (e.g., to [`3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L93)) pushes the model towards more deterministic paths, resulting in higher designability but reduced diversity in the generated outputs. Conversely, decreasing it allows for greater exploration of the latent space, increasing diversity. Similarly, [`inference_sampler.gamma_0`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/designability_vs_diversity.md#L8), which defaults to [`0.6`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L61), modulates the amount of noise introduced at each denoising step. Lowering [`gamma_0`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L37) (e.g., to [`0.2`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L33)) reduces randomness, favoring more probable and thus potentially more designable structures, at the expense of diversity. These settings are applied via the command-line interface during inference, as detailed in the RFD3 documentation, particularly in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/designability_vs_diversity.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/designability_vs_diversity.md) and [RFD3 Input Specification and Conditioning](#rfdiffusion3-rfd3-for-de-novo-design-rfd3-input-specification-and-conditioning). Practical examples of how these parameters affect design outcomes, especially in protein-protein interface design, are provided in documents like [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/protein_binder_design.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/protein_binder_design.md).

Another key control for influencing designability versus diversity lies in the [`is_non_loopy`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L191) setting within the input JSON/YAML configuration. When [`is_non_loopy`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L191) is set to [`True`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L175), the model is encouraged to generate structures with more defined secondary structure elements and fewer unstructured loop regions. This tends to increase the designability of the generated proteins, as structured proteins are often more stable and predictable. However, this preference for structured designs can lead to a slight reduction in the diversity of novel structural motifs explored. This setting is particularly relevant in tutorials such as [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/tutorials/binder_design_tutorial.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/tutorials/binder_design_tutorial.md) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/protein_binder_design.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/examples/protein_binder_design.md), where the creation of robust protein binders is often a primary goal. The document [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/designability_vs_diversity.md`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/designability_vs_diversity.md) offers visual examples illustrating the impact of these settings on design output characteristics, including metrics related to refolding pass rates and structural clustering.

### RFD3 Training Pipeline and Conditioning Strategies
The RFD3 training pipeline is primarily managed by the [`train`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/train.py#L26) function in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/train.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/train.py), which leverages [`hydra`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L27) for configuration and [`lightning.fabric`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L84) for distributed training. This setup allows for flexible experimentation and scalable training across multiple hardware configurations. The pipeline initializes a [`RankedLogger`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/utils/ddp.py#L58) for managing distributed logging and uses [`instantiate_loggers`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/utils/instantiators.py#L47) and [`instantiate_callbacks`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/utils/instantiators.py#L19) to dynamically set up monitoring and workflow automation.

Central to RFD3's training is the [`AADesignTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33) located in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py). This trainer orchestrates the model's forward and backward passes, loss calculations, and metric computations specific to protein design tasks. It extends the abstract [`FabricTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/src/foundry/trainers/fabric.py#L56) (see [Training Harness with PyTorch Lightning Fabric](#foundry-core-library-and-ml-workflows-training-harness-with-pytorch-lightning-fabric)) to handle the lifecycle of training and validation loops, ensuring consistent behavior in distributed environments.

A key aspect of RFD3's training is its sophisticated conditioning strategy, which creates diverse design problems during training. This involves fixing specific "motif tokens," atoms, sequences, or coordinates within a structure, guided by [`training_conditions`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L171) specified in the configuration files under [`global_transform_args`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L171). These conditions, processed by data transforms in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms), enable the model to learn to generate novel structures under various constraints. For instance, [`_assemble_network_inputs`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/trainers/rf3.py#L111) within [`AADesignTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33) is responsible for preparing and validating these conditioned inputs for the model, ensuring data integrity with checks for NaNs and consistent tensor shapes. The training process also incorporates a recycling schedule, managed by [`get_recycle_schedule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/recycling.py#L7) from [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/recycling.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/recycling.py), which defines the number of recycling steps per batch for distributed training, enhancing model performance and stability.

### RFD3 Core Model Components and Data Transformations
The RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) model, implemented primarily within the [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3) directory, is a generative diffusion model designed for *de novo* biomolecular interaction design. At its core, the [`RFD3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py#L19) class in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py) integrates several components: a [`TokenInitializer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L36) for feature preparation, a [`diffusion_module`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L241) responsible for denoising, and an [`inference_sampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54) ([`ConditionalDiffusionSampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L582)) to manage the iterative sampling process during inference. This modular design allows for flexible configuration and clear separation of concerns between input feature generation, the core denoising logic, and the multi-step diffusion sampling. The model supports conditional diffusion, where generation can be guided by input features, and incorporates classifier-free guidance during inference to enhance sample quality.

Neural network building blocks are located in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers). This collection provides various attention mechanisms, such as [`GatedCrossAttention`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/attention.py#L92) and [`LocalAttentionPairBias`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/attention.py#L189), which are crucial for processing atomic and token-level features, often incorporating pairwise biases for detailed structural interactions. Feature embedding layers like [`PositionPairDistEmbedder`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L66) and [`OneDFeatureEmbedder`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L116) are used to transform input data, while components like [`Upcast`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L465) and [`Downcast`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L514) manage the conversion between atom-level and token-level representations. For memory efficiency with large structures, specialized modules like [`ChunkedPairwiseEmbedder`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/chunked_pairwise.py#L142) perform calculations only on relevant subsets of data. Encoder blocks, such as [`TokenInitializer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L36) and [`DiffusionTokenEncoder`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/encoders.py#L304), refine these features, often integrating diffusion-specific information like distograms. These layers leverage performance optimizations such as activation checkpointing and mixed-precision training.

A comprehensive set of [`Transform`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L453) classes, found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms), handles the preparation of [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) data for both training and inference. These transformations manage conditioning by extracting motif information and setting default annotations via the transforms in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py). They apply design-specific featurization, such as creating reference features and adding boolean flags ([`is_backbone`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/pipelines.py#L504), [`is_sidechain`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py#L104), [`is_virtual`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py#L103)) using transforms in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/design_transforms.py). Hydrogen bond calculations are performed by transforms in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds.py) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/hbonds_hbplus.py), supporting both Biotite's internal functions and external tools like HBPLUS. Other transformations include cropping for protein-DNA contacts using transforms in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/dna_crop.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/dna_crop.py), chirality manipulations using transforms in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/ncaa_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/ncaa_transforms.py), and RASA calculation using transforms in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/rasa.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/rasa.py). The [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/pipelines.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/pipelines.py) module defines how these individual transforms are composed into comprehensive data processing workflows, often applying transformations conditionally based on whether the process is inference or training. For further details on the training process, see [RFD3 Training Pipeline and Conditioning Strategies](#rfdiffusion3-rfd3-for-de-novo-design-rfd3-training-pipeline-and-conditioning-strategies). The inference engine's operation is detailed in [RFD3 Inference and Design Examples](#rfdiffusion3-rfd3-for-de-novo-design-rfd3-inference-and-design-examples).

### RFD3 Metrics, Utilities, and Testing
RFdiffusion3 (RFD3) employs a range of metrics and utilities to assess *de novo* biomolecular designs, manage data, and support the inference process, ensuring that generated structures align with design principles and can be effectively analyzed and visualized.

A variety of metrics quantify design quality, covering structural integrity, sequence composition, and specific interactions. For instance, the functions and classes within [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/design_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/design_metrics.py) calculate clash metrics to identify unfavorable atomic overlaps, detect chain breaks, and assess secondary structure elements like helices, strands, and coils. This module also evaluates sequence recovery by comparing predicted sequences against ground truth, and analyzes protein-protein interaction (PPI) hotspots to determine if diffused atoms correctly contact critical regions. The [`AtomArrayMetrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/design_metrics.py#L170) class, found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/design_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/design_metrics.py), further provides general structural and compositional statistics, including the radius of gyration and amino acid content.

Hydrogen bond quantification is addressed by [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_metrics.py) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_hbplus_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_hbplus_metrics.py). These modules process [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) objects to identify hydrogen bonds and evaluate the accuracy of predicted donors and acceptors against ground truth, providing metrics on the percentage of correctly predicted H-bonds and their total count. They incorporate preprocessing steps, such as [`simplified_processing_atom_array`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/hbonds_metrics.py#L26), to ensure accurate residue identification and handle virtual atoms, which is crucial for reliable H-bond calculations.

Sidechain quality is assessed by [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/sidechain_metrics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/sidechain_metrics.py). This includes functions like [`collapsing_virtual_atoms_batched`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/sidechain_metrics.py#L9) to identify and remove virtual atoms that indicate collapsed sidechains, and [`check_sidechain_quality`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/sidechain_metrics.py#L114) which compares the topology of generated sidechains to standard amino acid structures using graph-based methods. It also identifies unintended bonds between sidechains of different residues and intra-residue clashes.

Loss functions are defined in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py), which includes [`SequenceLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/metrics/losses.py#L7) for token-level cross-entropy on sequence predictions and [`DiffusionLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) for coordinate-based mean squared error. The [`DiffusionLoss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L416) can incorporate an optional [`smoothed_lddt_loss`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/loss/af3_losses.py#L544), which measures structural similarity by comparing inter-atomic distances. These loss functions are critical for guiding model training.

Beyond metrics, the RFD3 framework includes utilities for [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) preparation, I/O operations, and visualization. The [`inference`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/mpnn/README.md#L120) utility in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/utils/inference.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/utils/inference.py) assists with [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) preparation and structural patching, while the [`io`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/.env#L57) utility in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/utils/io.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/utils/io.py) handles saving generated structures, metadata, and trajectories. For visualizing results, the [`vizualize`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L284) utility in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/utils/vizualize.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/utils/vizualize.py) provides functions for PyMOL. The comprehensive [`pytest`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L295) suite, located in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/tests`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/tests), ensures the correctness and consistency of these components, covering core functionality, bond preservation, conditioning logic, pipeline equivalence, and symmetry properties.

## RFdiffusion3NA (RFD3NA) for Multipolymer Design
RFdiffusion3NA (RFD3NA) is a framework designed for *de novo* biomolecular design, specifically extending the capabilities of RFDiffusion3 to multipolymer systems including proteins, DNA, and RNA. The framework supports the design of complex structures with atomic functional sites, offering comprehensive tools for model definition, training, inference, and evaluation.

Installation involves installing the [`rc-foundry[rfd3na]`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/README.md#L20) package and downloading necessary checkpoints, managed through commands like [`pip install rc-foundry[rfd3na]`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/README.md#L134) and [`foundry install rfd3na`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L1).

For inference, the [`rfd3na design`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L1) command-line interface facilitates running design tasks. Users can define multipolymer [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) regions, specifying protein, RNA, or DNA chains (e.g., [`10-10,20-20R,30-30D`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/README.md#L55)). This process is managed by the [`RFD3InferenceEngine`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L140) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/engine.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/engine.py), which handles input processing and model execution to generate [`RFD3Output`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L92). Advanced control over the inference process is available through options such as [`dump_trajectories`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/src/rf3/utils/io.py#L141) for debugging, [`prevalidate_inputs`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L71) for input validation, and [`skip_existing`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L51) to manage output files.

RFD3NA incorporates hydrogen bond conditioning during design. This functionality leverages external tools like [`HBPLUS`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/README.md#L143), which requires specific configuration of its path via an environment variable.

The framework also supports training and fine-tuning. The main entry point for this is the script in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/train.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/train.py), which utilizes [`hydra`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L27) for configuration and [`lightning.fabric`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L84) for distributed execution. Training involves complex conditioning strategies, where the model learns from a variety of generated "problems" that fix specific atoms, sequences, or coordinates. This allows for diverse design scenarios. The [`AADesignTrainer`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/trainer/rfd3.py#L33) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/trainer/rfd3na.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/trainer/rfd3na.py) extends a generic trainer to manage the specific steps involved in design training, including network input assembly and output generation. The training process can be monitored with various logging options, including Weights & Biases or CSV.

The core model implementation, located in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/model`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/model), features the [`RFD3`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3.py#L19) class, which integrates a [`diffusion_module`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L241) (an [`RFD3DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L32)) and an [`inference_sampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54) ([`ConditionalDiffusionSampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/inference_sampler.py#L582)). The [`RFD3DiffusionModule`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/RFD3_diffusion_module.py#L32) employs a UNet-like architecture for denoising coordinates and sequence features. The [`inference_sampler`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/engine.py#L54) supports controlled, iterative denoising, including classifier-free guidance and symmetry application.

The framework also provides extensive data transformation capabilities in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms). These [`Transform`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L453) classes preprocess [`biotite.structure.AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/docs/input.md#L124) objects, handling conditioning strategies, feature generation, hydrogen bond calculations, and symmetry integration to ensure structural integrity during multipolymer design.

Finally, RFD3NA includes a comprehensive suite of metrics in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/metrics`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/metrics) for evaluating design quality. These metrics assess aspects such as clashes, chain breaks, backbone metrics, protein-protein interface (PPI) characteristics, sequence recovery, nucleic acid secondary structure similarity (using F1 scores), and ligand contacts, guiding the training process and informing the quality of generated designs.

### RFD3NA Input Specification and Multipolymer Contigs
RFdiffusion3NA (RFD3NA) employs a specialized input system to manage complex multipolymer designs, enabling users to define regions for design, impose structural constraints, and specify interactions. This system facilitates the generation of diverse biomolecular architectures involving proteins, DNA, and RNA.

A central element of RFD3NA's input system is the [`contig`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L134) specification, which allows for defining continuous regions of polymers to be designed or preserved. Unlike single-polymer systems, RFD3NA extends this to multipolymer types, such as [`10-10,20-20R,30-30D`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/README.md#L55), where [`P`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/pyproject.toml#L112) (or no suffix) denotes protein, [`R`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/README.md#L161) denotes RNA, and [`D`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L392) denotes DNA. This syntax allows for precise control over the composition and length of different polymer chains within a single design problem. The system processes these specifications, along with [`length`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L141) constraints and [`unindex`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L135) tokens, to delineate designable and fixed regions. These specifications are validated and prepared by the [`DesignInputSpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L115) class, found in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/input_parsing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/input_parsing.py), which ensures internal consistency and handles the transformation of user input into a machine-readable format. For backwards compatibility, a [`LegacySpecification`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L80) in [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/legacy_input_parsing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/legacy_input_parsing.py) exists to process older input formats. The [`accumulate_components`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L1287) function, critical to both new and legacy parsing, constructs the initial molecular structure by combining motif regions from existing structures and newly generated diffused residues, managing chain breaks and polymer type assignments.

Beyond contig specification, RFD3NA offers a flexible [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) mini-language for specifying precise residue and atom selections. This capability allows users to designate specific atoms or residues for various conditioning tasks, such as fixing their coordinates ([`select_fixed_atoms`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L152)), controlling their sequence identity ([`select_unfixed_sequence`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L160)), or specifying their burial or exposure ([`select_buried`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L170), [`select_exposed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L172)). More advanced conditioning includes defining hotspots ([`select_hotspots`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L176)) for interaction interfaces and specifying hydrogen bond donors or acceptors ([`select_hbond_donor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L175), [`select_hbond_acceptor`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L174)). These selections are processed and applied as annotations to the [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20) data structure, enabling the model to incorporate these constraints during the diffusion process. The [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/parsing.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference/parsing.py) module handles the parsing and validation of these [`InputSelection`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/parsing.py#L26) objects, converting various input forms into canonicalized data dictionaries and masks.

For nucleic acid designs, RFD3NA integrates advanced constraints. This includes specifying nucleic acid secondary structure through parameters like [`ss_dbn`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L48), which supports dot-bracket notation, and defining paired or loop regions using [`paired_region_list`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L91), [`loop_region_list`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L92), and [`paired_position_list`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/docs/examples/atom23_design.md#L116). These features are crucial for guiding the design towards specific RNA or DNA folds and interactions. Ligand interactions can also be specified using the [`ligand`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L142) parameter, enabling the design of protein or nucleic acid binders to small molecules. Additionally, global conditioning flags like [`plddt_enhanced`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L190), [`is_non_loopy`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L191), and [`partial_t`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py#L193) allow for further control over the design process, such as enabling confidence-based design or partial diffusion from an existing structure.

The overall input management system, as implemented in the [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/inference) directory, provides the necessary tools for users to define complex multipolymer design problems. It transforms these high-level specifications into a structured representation that the diffusion model can interpret and act upon, forming the basis for diverse biomolecular engineering tasks.

### RFD3NA Data Transforms and Symmetry Operations
The RFD3NA framework leverages a comprehensive suite of data transformations to prepare molecular structures for multipolymer design, ensuring accurate representation and conditioning. These transformations are critical for tasks ranging from conditioning the diffusion process to generating specialized features and applying symmetry constraints.

A core aspect of this framework is the definition and application of various **conditioning strategies**. These strategies, implemented as [`Transform`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rf3/README.md#L453) classes, guide the model by specifying fixed regions, motifs, or designable areas within a molecular structure. Files such as [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/conditioning_base.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/conditioning_base.py) and [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/training_conditions.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/training_conditions.py) manage the global conditioning syntax. This includes [`IslandCondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L56) for selecting token "islands" as motifs, [`PPICondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L176) for defining protein-protein interaction interfaces, and [`SubtypeCondition`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/training_conditions.py#L272) for targeting specific molecular subtypes like protein, DNA, or RNA. These conditions dictate how annotations such as [`is_motif_atom_with_fixed_seq`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L9) (fixed sequence), [`is_motif_atom_with_fixed_coord`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L10) (fixed coordinates), and [`is_motif_atom_unindexed`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/constants.py#L11) (tokens whose positions are diffused) are applied to the [`AtomArray`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/examples/all.ipynb#L20). The [`UnindexFlaggedTokens`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/transforms/conditioning_base.py#L315) transform is particularly significant as it handles the expansion of unindexed motifs and generates [`unindexing_pair_mask`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3/src/rfd3/model/layers/blocks.py#L341) for relative positional encoding, ensuring proper information flow within the model.

**Feature generation** is another critical component, detailed within [`/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/design_transforms.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/foundry/models/rfd3na/src/rfd3na/transforms/design_transforms.py). These transforms create diverse molecular features essential for the model's predictive capabilities.
